figures.firstNativeObservation: Shared water-air surface, common S origin, central normal direction, seven prominent upward directions and two shallow outer transmissions are visible. Incident arrows face the interface; return branches face away below it, with stronger outer reflections and no upper continuation for the two outermost families per side. Pale water area replaces engraving. Source S and modern English labels are legible and unclipped at native resolution. Lower central reflection is superposed on the incident normal trace and needs the first actual mobile observation.

Nine complete concentric closed loops are drawn over nine horizontal strands that visibly continue directly from Input to Output. At the bottom the loop and straight portions merge and cross with no visible over/under separation or route distinction. The learner can follow a straight bypass without traversing the curved bundle, or read a closed ring attached to a bar. Two terminal faces and the hollow loop survive, but the source's single bent bundle route is not clearly preserved. Tangency and equal endpoint heights do not resolve that visual topology. English labels are legible and unclipped; there is no prism, right-angle ray-turn marker or optical ray inset.
